gloss: the other shore; the far bank; the opposite side

definitions.gloss: the other shore; the far bank; the opposite side of a river or body of water
definitions.explanation: The bank or shore on the opposite side of a river, lake, or other body of water from where the speaker is. Can also be used figuratively for something that feels distant or unreachable.

examples.japanese: {向|む}こう{岸|ぎし}に{人|ひと}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: I can see someone on the other shore.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}の{向|む}こう{岸|ぎし}まで{泳|およ}いで{渡|わた}った。
examples.english: I swam across to the other bank of the river.

examples.japanese: {向|む}こう{岸|ぎし}の{景色|けしき}が{夕日|ゆうひ}に{照|て}らされて、とても{美|うつく}しかった。
examples.english: The scenery on the far shore, lit up by the sunset, was very beautiful.

notes:
Compound of {向|む}こう (the other side; over there) + {岸|きし} (shore; bank). The reading changes to ぎし through {連濁|れんだく} (sequential voicing).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {向|む}こう{岸|ぎし}に{渡|わた}る: to cross to the other side
- {向|む}こう{岸|ぎし}が{見|み}える: the far shore is visible
- {川|かわ}の{向|む}こう{岸|ぎし}: the opposite bank of the river

USAGE:
Sometimes used metaphorically to mean something distant or out of reach, similar to "the other side" in English. In Buddhism, {彼岸|ひがん} (the other shore) represents enlightenment or the afterlife.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {対岸|たいがん}: the opposite bank — more formal and literary; often used in the expression {対岸|たいがん}の{火事|かじ} (someone else's problem, literally "a fire on the opposite bank")
- {彼岸|ひがん}: the other shore (Buddhist) — specifically refers to the Buddhist concept of the afterlife or enlightenment, or the equinox holiday period
